shorts.title: The Echidna Breaks the Biggest Rule of Being a Mammal 🦔
shorts.description:
This spiky animal breaks the biggest mammal rule. Echidnas have no nipples: the milk seeps from patches of skin inside the pouch.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Short-beaked echidna: CC0, Paul Coddington (CC BY), Wendy F (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What did you guess the rule was?

shorts.title: The Biggest Rodent on Earth Holds Its Breath 5 Minutes 🦫
shorts.description:
This is the biggest rodent on Earth. The Catholic Church once gave special permission to eat capybara during Lent.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

shorts.title: Blue-Footed Boobies Get Their Color From Fish 🐟
shorts.description:
These birds get blue feet from fish. 'Booby' comes from the Spanish 'bobo', for clumsy on land.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Blue-footed booby: gwar (CC BY), William Stephens (CC BY), John G. Phillips (CC BY), Anthony Batista (CC BY). creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: What color would your feet be?

shorts.title: Galápagos Tortoises Can Go a Year Without Food 🐢
shorts.description:
This tortoise can go a year without food. Lonesome George, the last Pinta Island tortoise, died on 24 June 2012.

#shorts #animalfacts #meatballmyths

Photos (iNaturalist), cropped and color-adjusted: Galápagos tortoise: Carrie Seltzer (CC BY), CC0. creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0 · creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0
shorts.comment: How long could you go without snacks?
